summary: The eval seam hands a dream adaptor the batch size the DEPLOYMENT gives it, asked of the runtime, instead of a hardcoded 64 for every adaptor.
details: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by the new per-run spend line: a note_candidates case emitted ~7,157 output tokens per model call against production's measured median of 711 (104 completions, Langfuse). The eval was handing every adaptor 64 rows while composition gives note-candidates 80 (composition.py:3177) and culture 300 (:3247).
A tier PRESENT but REDUCED is the same divergence as one absent -- design/evaluation/11-the-sandbox-rebuild.md §6 R7 -- and this one was invisible because both numbers are plausible batch sizes.

`DreamerRuntime.batch_limit_for(name)` is the third of the per-adaptor accessors the runtime already exposes (`samples_for`, `max_items_for`) and reads the same `AdaptorSchedule.batch_limit` field `nora/app/runtime.py`'s `_dream_adaptor_once` reads. `nora.subject.dream(limit=None)` now asks instead of assuming; an explicit `limit` still wins for a caller deliberately probing a smaller window.
This also explains the truncations seen the same day: a call emitting ~7,000 tokens did not fit the then-6,000 per-call ceiling.
